The leaking compression joint was confirmed by the contractor and the tenant (event-009, event-010), and the leak recurred on 13 June when the tap was used (event-020). The joint cannot be reached through the hatch. The contractor found an unidentified fibrous lining behind the ceiling board, paused, and left without opening it (event-017, event-023). We told him not to disturb the lining (event-018). No survey or alteration records exist (event-006, event-013, event-022). A young child lives in the flat (event-007). The landlord's authority covers the quoted plumbing scope only. She has refused to extend it to a material assessment without cost and timing (event-013, event-022). The contractor cannot price that assessment (event-023). We have no authority to approve spend, and there is no quote to route for approval, so ROUTE_FOR_APPROVAL does not fit. WAIT is wrong because the leak is active and the landlord decision was already requested (event-024). I set P1 because the leak is ongoing, a child is present and the material is unidentified. I did not set P0 because the tenant reports no electrical impact, no sagging and a small drip only, and the tap is out of use (event-003, event-020). This would become P0 if the drip worsens, the ceiling sags, or water reaches electrics. No attachments exist and no instruction in the case tried to change our process.

actions.summary: 16 Brindlewick Mews: the kitchen ceiling leak from a compression joint is recurring and the repair is blocked. An unidentified fibrous lining sits behind the ceiling board, and nobody can say whether it is hazardous. A young child lives in the flat. The landlord authorised the plumbing scope only and wants cost and timing for any assessment, which we cannot supply yet.
known: Tenant reported damp patch and drips on 10 June (event-001); no electrics affected, no sagging (event-003).
Mossbarrow Pipe Services saw moisture at a compression joint above the hatch with the tap running; the joint is unreachable through the hatch (event-009, event-011).

Landlord authorised the quoted plumbing scope only, up to the estimate, and asked to be told before any scope or cost increase (event-013). On 13 June she confirmed that this does not cover a specialist material assessment and asked for likely cost and timing (event-022).

On 13 June Kellan saw a pale fibrous-looking lining behind the board, could not identify it, and paused (event-017). We told him not to disturb it or drill, cut, sample or remove (event-018). He left without opening the ceiling (event-023).
Tenant reported a small drip when the tap was used on the morning of 13 June, has stopped using that tap, and the ceiling is not sagging (event-020). A young child will be present (event-007).
No survey or ceiling alteration records exist from the landlord or the building manager (event-006, event-013, event-022).
Event-024 asked the landlord for a decision on further assessment or repair scope; no extra cost or appointment is agreed.
Request: Please arrange an inspection of a damp patch and occasional dripping from the kitchen ceiling. The patch has returned after rain. (request)
unknowns: What the lining is, and whether it contains asbestos.
Cost and timing of a specialist assessment, and who should provide it.
Whether the landlord will authorise an assessment and the later repair.
Whether the leak is getting worse, and how long the isolated tap can stay out of use.
Cost and timing of an assessment
tried: Asked the building manager for records (event-005, event-006).
Asked the landlord for survey records and authorisation (event-012, event-013).
Paused the contractor and kept the ceiling undisturbed (event-018).
Told the tenant not to touch the hatch and to report any new dripping (event-019).
Asked the landlord for a decision on further scope (event-024).
options: Recommended: Ask the landlord to approve a specialist surveyor attending or quoting for identification of the lining, then route the quote for approval; give the landlord an interim cost and timing indication once known.

Ask the landlord for approval to use a licensed contractor who can isolate the supply or make a temporary non-invasive control of the leak, without disturbing the lining, while the assessment is arranged.
Keep the tenant updated, tell them to keep the tap out of use, and report any worsening drip, sagging or electrical effect at once for re-triage to P0.
